Hi, 
I am using the newest version of dartR (2.0.4).
I have a question on the 2 functions "gl.report.hwe" & "gl.filter.hwe".

I have run "gl.report.hwe" on my dataset in the following way:
<
gl.report.hwe(
            my_gl_dataset,
            subset = "each", #  loci sign out of HWE at any population = "OUT ANY"; 
            method_sig = "Exact",
            multi_comp = FALSE,
            multi_comp_method = "BY",
            alpha_val = 0.05,
            pvalue_type = "midp",
            cc_val = 0.5,
            sig_only = TRUE,
            min_sample_size = 5, 
            plot.out = TRUE,
            max_plots = 4,
            save2tmp = FALSE,
            verbose = NULL
          ) 
>

--> With this report, I get only 1 locus (942-23-C/T) that seem to be out of HWE at all populations (npop) (my tot # pop = 12 & npop = 12). -->
Q1. Is that correct?
Q2. Why the parameters for this locus are reported only in 5 populations (f,d,g,h,i) instead than for all the 12 populations in which this locus is out of HWE? (Same issue for the other loci above reported out of HWE in additional populations to the one listed)

Population -     Locus     - Hom_1 - Het - Hom_2 - N -     Prob - Sig - Prob.adj - Sig.adj - npop
               a     272-15-G/A    35           1          1        37      4.1e-02 sig       NA          NA        4
                b    783-14-C/T   16            0          1       17      3.0e-02 sig       NA           NA       5
                c    783-14-C/T   22            0          1        23      2.2e-02 sig       NA           NA      5
                d    902-51-T/A    44            0          1        45      1.1e-02 sig       NA           NA      8
                e    546-67-G/A    31            1          1        33      4.6e-02 sig       NA           NA      5
---                                                                                                  
                f     942-23-C/T    12            4           8        24     1.9e-03 sig       NA           NA     12
                d    942-23-C/T    31             1          4        36     4.4e-05 sig       NA           NA     12
                g    942-23-C/T    37             0           1       38      1.3e-02 sig       NA           NA     12
                h    942-23-C/T     8               2          6       16       3.0e-03 sig       NA           NA    12
                 i    942-23-C/T    13              0          1       14       3.7e-02 sig       NA           NA    12

So from this output table from the "gl.report.hwe", I understand that there are 5 loci in total (272-15-G/A, 783-14-C/T,  902-51-T/A, 546-67-G/A, 942-23-C/T) that are out of HWE. --> 
Q3. Is that correct?

I then run the "gl.filter.hwe", with the same tests parameters (Exact test, alfa 0.05), like this:
<
my_gl_dataset_HWE = gl.filter.hwe(
            my_gl_dataset,
            subset = "each",
            n.pop.threshold = 12, # --> I ask to remove loci only if out of HWE in all pops?
            method_sig = "Exact",
            multi_comp = FALSE,
            multi_comp_method = "BY",
            alpha_val = 0.05,
            pvalue_type = "midp",
            cc_val = 0.5,
            min_sample_size = 5,
            verbose = NULL
          ) 
>

Result:
Loci examined: 22550
  Deleted 106 loci with significant departure from HWE at alpha = 0.05 applied locus by locus
  Loci retained: 22444


Q4. Are all the loci detected as out of HWE reported in the table output of the "gl.report.hwe" function? Why then, when I run the "gl.filter.hwe" function with the same test type and alfa value 106 loci out of HWE are deleted  instead of the only 5 loci reported by the "gl.report.hwe" function?

I would really appreciate some clarifications on the different results of the 2 functions and some feedback on whether I am interpreting the outputs of these functions correctly.
Thank you so much as usual for all your assistance!
Best,
Gabriella

parts:
Hi Gabriella,

The table produced by gl.report.hwe() is a data.table object, see more information here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/data.table/vignettes/datatable-intro.html.

A data.table object is in almost all aspects the same as a data.frame object. One of the differences is that a data.table when printed, only the beginning and end of the object are displayed. To displayed the first 100 rows of the data.table you could use:
library(dartR)
test <- platypus.gl
res <- gl.report.hwe(test)
print(res,topn  = 100)

I think, this solves Q1 to Q4.

Your interpretation from Q5 is correct.

Cheers,
Luis

Hi Gabriella,

Thank you for reporting this bug.

The issue was that the step of counting the number of populations in which loci are significant was performed, funny enough, before actually removing the loci that are significant.

This bug did not affect the gl.filter.hwe function.

Now gl.report.hwe reports correctly the number of population in which loci are significant, see code below.

To use this updated version of the function, you should install the developing version of dartR, as shown in the code below.

Cheers,
Luis

library(dartR)
# installing the developing version of dartR
gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "dev")
# test dataset
test <- platypus.gl
# HWE report
report_hwe <- gl.report.hwe(test)
# subsetting loci that are significant in all populations
report_pop <- report_hwe[which(report_hwe$npop==nPop(test)),]
# getting unique loci names and counting them
length(unique(report_pop$Locus))
# [1] 17

# Filtering loci in HWE.
res <- gl.filter.hwe(test,
                     subset = "each",
                     n.pop.threshold = nPop(test))

# 17 loci filtered
 nLoc(test) - nLoc(res)
